plan.title: 3-group liver DE: LRT + treated-vs-control contrasts
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is raw gene-level Salmon counts for 12 human liver samples in three groups (control, treated_a, treated_b, 4 replicates each, unpaired, single batch) in counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 sample columns + gene-symbol column), with condition labels in metadata.csv. The research question has two parts: (1) which genes differ across the three groups at all, and (2) which genes each treatment changes relative to control. A three-group design with replicated groups calls for the DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (full ~condition vs reduced ~1) to answer the any-difference question, followed by one named Wald contrast per treatment against the explicitly set reference level 'control', with ashr shrinkage of the reported log2 fold changes (contrasts are not single coefficients, so apeglm does not apply) and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment within each contrast. An edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts serves as the second method for robustness; with 4 replicates per group the two methods disagree on some genes, so the report treats the intersection as the high-confidence set. Normalization stays inside the models (median-of-ratios size factors for DESeq2, TMM for edgeR) — no pre-normalization. Sample structure QC (blind vst, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) runs before any test. The question asks nothing about pathways or regulators, so no enrichment or TF-activity step is planned.

steps.method: vst blind + PCA + sample distance heatmap
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (full ~condition vs reduced ~1) then pairwise Wald contrasts vs reference
DE report with methods, design, thresholds, diagnostics, reproducibility record
